text: Deep learning is a subset of machine learning that is based on artificial neural networks with representation learning. Scholarly analysis indicates that the adjective deep in deep learning refers to the utilize of multiple layers in the network. Historically, neural networks were limited in depth due to computational constraints and training difficulties. Today, modern deep learning architectures utilize convolutional neural networks and transformer architectures to process vast datasets. In this paper, we introduce an empirical evaluation of lexical and semantic document similarity metrics to assist researchers in maintaining manuscript originality.

text:
Smart India Hackathon 2026
Complete Problem Statement Guide — Software + Hardware
All problem statements captured from the SIH 2026 catalogue (226 total — 172 Software, 54
Hardware), organized by theme, with a legend distinguishing Software vs Hardware tracks, plus a
strategic recommendation for the strongest hardware+software project to build.
SW
= Software track
HW
= Hardware track
Source: SIH 2026 Official Master Catalogue — compiled from a third-party mirror of sih.gov.in data. Some theme tags in the raw source
appeared inconsistent; verify final picks on sih.gov.in/sih2026PS.
Prepared: August 2026

A Note on the Data
This guide is built from a third-party compiled mirror of the SIH 2026 catalogue, not scraped directly from sih.gov.in (which
blocks automated access). Titles here are shortened for table readability — the official portal has the full problem statement
text, background, and expected solution for each code. Verify your shortlisted PS number's exact title, theme, and full
description on sih.gov.in/sih2026PS before finalizing your choice.
All Problem Statements by Theme
Both SOFTWARE and HARDWARE tracks are included below. Rows are shaded blue (Software) or red (Hardware) for
quick scanning.

Recommendation: Best Bets for a Hardware + Software Build
Ranked for a 6-member student team building a genuine hardware + software solution, weighing feasibility in the
hackathon timeframe, demo strength, and alignment with what SIH judging panels tend to reward.
■ 1st Choice — SIH26025: Mine Subsidence Monitoring & Early Warning System
Theme: Disaster Management  |  Ministry of Coal  |  Track: Hardware
The strongest overall pick. Disaster Management is the largest theme in the catalogue, which typically means
ministries and evaluators invest heavily in that track. The hardware is realistically buildable in a hackathon: tilt/vibration
sensors and strain gauges wired to an ESP32 or Arduino, transmitting over LoRa or GSM from a small test rig
simulating a mine wall. The software layer — a predictive ML model over the sensor time-series, a live dashboard, and
automated SMS/app alerts — is exactly the AI + IoT combination judges reward. It's demonstrable live on stage: shake
the rig, watch the alert fire in real time.
■ 2nd Choice — SIH26177: AI-Powered Search-and-Rescue Drone
Theme: Disaster Management  |  Sponsor: Qualcomm Inc  |  Track: Hardware
Highest "wow factor" of the shortlist. You don't need a fully flying drone to prove the concept — a tethered quadcopter
or a small ground rover with a camera running person/hazard detection (YOLO on a Jetson Nano or Raspberry Pi)
makes for a compelling demo. Qualcomm-sponsored problem statements often come with access to dev kits and
technical support, a practical edge during the build phase.
■ 3rd Choice — SIH26109: Bovine Mastitis Early Forecasting
Theme: Agriculture, FoodTech & Rural Development  |  Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying  |  Track: Hardware
Less crowded — far fewer teams gravitate toward a dairy-sensor problem compared to AI chatbots or vision systems,
which can work in your favor for differentiation and evaluator attention. The hardware is simple (a milk
conductivity/temperature sensor) paired with an ML classification model, and the rural impact story is strong for the
pitch.
Why the top pick wins
Winning SIH is less about picking the flashiest idea and more about picking a problem your team can fully close the
loop on — working hardware, working software, and a live, convincing demo — within the time you have. SIH26025
lets a 6-person team split cleanly: 2 on embedded/sensors, 2 on backend/ML, 2 on dashboard/frontend + pitch, with no
single point of failure (no drone-flight risk, no exotic hardware to source).
Next Steps
1
Verify your shortlisted PS number, exact title, and full description on sih.gov.in/sih2026PS before committing.
2
Confirm team composition against SIH rules: exactly 6 students, same college, minimum 1 female member.
3
Draft a system architecture (sensor stack → data pipeline → ML model → dashboard/alerting) for your chosen PS.
4
Build a rough 36-hour execution timeline splitting hardware, backend, and frontend/pitch work across the team.

Recommendation: Best Bets for a Hardware + Software Build
Ranked for a 6-member student team building a genuine hardware + software solution, weighing feasibility in the
hackathon timeframe, demo strength, and alignment with what SIH judging panels tend to reward.

■ 1st Choice — SIH26025: Mine Subsidence Monitoring & Early Warning System
Theme: Disaster Management  |  Ministry of Coal  |  Track:

Hardware
The strongest overall pick.

Disaster Management is the largest theme in the catalogue, which typically means
ministries and evaluators invest heavily in that track.

The hardware is realistically buildable in a hackathon: tilt/vibration
sensors and strain gauges wired to an ESP32 or Arduino, transmitting over LoRa or GSM from a small test rig
simulating a mine wall.

The software layer — a predictive ML model over the sensor time-series, a live dashboard, and
automated SMS/app alerts — is exactly the AI + IoT combination judges reward.

It's demonstrable live on stage: shake
the rig, watch the alert fire in real time.

■ 2nd Choice — SIH26177: AI-Powered Search-and-Rescue Drone
Theme: Disaster Management  |  Sponsor: Qualcomm Inc  |

Track: Hardware
Highest "wow factor" of the shortlist.

You don't need a fully flying drone to prove the concept — a tethered quadcopter
or a small ground rover with a camera running person/hazard detection (YOLO on a Jetson Nano or Raspberry Pi)
makes for a compelling demo.

Qualcomm-sponsored problem statements often come with access to dev kits and
technical support, a practical edge during the build phase.

■ 3rd Choice — SIH26109: Bovine Mastitis Early Forecasting
Theme: Agriculture, FoodTech & Rural Development  |  Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying

|  Track: Hardware
Less crowded — far fewer teams gravitate toward a dairy-sensor problem compared to AI chatbots or vision systems,
which can work in your favor for differentiation and evaluator attention.

The hardware is simple (a milk
conductivity/temperature sensor) paired with an ML classification model, and the rural impact story is strong for the
pitch.

Why the top pick wins
Winning SIH is less about picking the flashiest idea and more about picking a problem your team can fully close the
loop on — working hardware, working software, and a live, convincing demo — within the time you have.

SIH26025
lets a 6-person team split cleanly: 2 on embedded/sensors, 2 on backend/ML, 2 on dashboard/frontend + pitch, with no
single point of failure (no drone-flight risk, no exotic hardware to source).

Next Steps
1
Verify your shortlisted PS number, exact title, and full description on sih.gov.in/sih2026PS before committing.

2
Confirm team composition against SIH rules: exactly 6 students, same college, minimum 1 female member.

3
Draft a system architecture (sensor stack → data pipeline → ML model → dashboard/alerting) for your chosen PS.
4
Build a rough 36-hour execution timeline splitting hardware, backend, and frontend/pitch work across the team.
